translation.text: Wisdom found no place where she could dwell, and her dwelling was in the heavens.

translation.text: Wisdom went out to dwell among humankind, but she found no dwelling place. Wisdom returned to her place and took her seat among the angels.[a]

footnotes.text: The starred verb can involve taking a seat or mounting; “took her seat” follows its seating sense. The source does not name a throne or a vehicle, and neither is added here.

translation.text: Unrighteousness went out from her storehouses. She found those she had stirred to desire[a] and dwelt among them, like rain in a wilderness and dew upon thirsty ground.

footnotes.text: The selected clause is positive and contains the prefixed form አፈቀደት. The basic verb can mean seek or desire; its causative can mean cause someone to desire. The provisional rendering “those she had stirred to desire” follows that causative possibility, but the precise relative-object construction and what is desired remain uncertain. A negative such as “those who did not seek her” is not printed here.

translation.text: I saw other flashes of lightning and the stars of heaven. I saw how he calls them all by their names, and they hear him.

translation.text: I saw their just weighing—how they are weighed by their lights, according to the breadth of their places[a] and the day of their existence. Their revolution brings forth lightning,[b] and their revolution is according to the number of the angels.[c] They keep faith with one another.

footnotes.text: Charles records an initial-letter emendation in the breadth expression in printed page84 note12. This source preserves the selected initial ለ rather than the raw OCR’s ሰ.

“Revolution” follows the astronomical turning sense of the noun. The compressed lightning and birth clause is provisionally related to that motion; its precise subject and object require further review. “Day of their existence” stays close to the printed expression without adding a more exact astronomical interpretation.
The selected text says “angels,” not “stars.” The wording is retained rather than silently harmonized to the surrounding discussion of stars.

translation.text: I asked the angel who travelled with me and showed me what is hidden, “What are these?”
